confirmed.summary: mutate_identifier_swap produces syntactically invalid garbage mutants: _ID_RE includes apostrophes so it absorbs closing quotes of string literals, and the incomplete KEYWORDS set lets keywords be swapped with identifiers.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified against the shipped code: `print('result', count)` mutates to `result'('print, count)` (the match `result'` carries the string's closing quote, leaving unbalanced quoting), and `raise ValueError('expected positive count')` mutates to `ValueError raise(...)` because 'raise' (also elif/except/assert/sizeof/typedef/throw/catch...) is missing from KEYWORDS. These mutants are blatant syntax errors, not 'stylistically plausible single-site bugs'; the model is maximally surprised by them at zero context, so they add a large depth-independent component to the id_swap delta-bits signal, flattening the depth-dependence the anomaly probe exists to measure — silently, since they are recorded as ordinary id_swap mutants in the meta. Common in Python/JS corpora where single-quoted strings and un-listed keywords appear on most lines.

verdicts.reasoning: CONFIRMED by mechanical execution of the shipped code. Bonus confirmed mode: words inside string literals match _ID_RE and get swapped with code identifiers. Downstream impact is as claimed: id_swap is the most permissive mutator (any line with 2+ non-keyword identifiers), pick_sites accepts a line if ANY mutator fires, the meta rows (anomaly.py:223-231) record kind="id_swap" with no validity flag, and plot_anomaly (leanscale/plots.py:76) pools ALL kinds into one mean-delta_bits-per-depth curve per language — so a large, locally-driven, depth-independent surprise component from syntax-error mutants contaminates the pooled anomaly curve and dilutes the depth-dependence the probe exists to measure. Python and JavaScript are in the shipped LANGUAGES config and single-quoted strings plus un-listed keywords appear on a large fraction of eligible lines, so this hits the running anomaly sweep, silently. Severity "major" is fair under the stated rubric (silently degrades the science of the anomaly cross-check).

confirmed.summary: is_code_line only rejects lines that START with a comment marker, so mutation sites land inside docstring/block-comment interiors, and mutators edit trailing comments and string-literal contents — producing 'mutants' that are not code bugs at all.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified: Python docstring interior lines like '    The result includes the first 3 warmup steps and both counters.' return True from is_code_line (they don't start with '#'), and id_swap/off_by_one fire on prose (any line with two 3+-char words, or a digit). Same for Lean /-! ... -/ doc-block interiors and C block-comment bodies not starting with '*'. Mid-line cases too: off_by_one mutated '# retry up to 3 times' in a trailing comment and 'expected 2 args' inside a format string; cmp_swap mutated 'count <= 0' inside a die("...") message. Since pick_sites takes the FIRST passing line at each depth, a nontrivial fraction of anomaly sites per window are prose/comment/string edits whose surprisal has nothing to do with bug detection, diluting and biasing the depth-vs-delta-bits curve toward a null result — silently, as meta labels them like real code mutations.

confirmed.summary: Variants-mode PREFIX decodes request logits for every token although only the last prefix token's logits are consumed, wasting roughly a quarter of the decode compute across the anomaly and ablation stages.
confirmed.failure_scenario: decode_range sets batch.logits[k]=1 unconditionally; run_variants only reads the logits row of the final chunk token (to seed last_logits). For Qwen2-0.5B the 151936x896 lm_head is ~28% of per-token FLOPs, so computing logits for ~13-15K prefix tokens per job across ~36 anomaly jobs plus 16 ablation jobs burns roughly 45-60 minutes of the chained 4-core CPU budget (each 16K-token decode already measures ~250s) and forces a 512x151936 float output buffer (~311MB), for zero measurement benefit. Full mode legitimately needs all logits; variants mode should enable logits only on each chunk's last token.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed mechanically. tools/ppl_dump.cpp:104 sets batch.logits[k]=1 for every token in decode_range regardless of mode. In run_variants, the PREFIX callback (lines 181-186) consumes only the row where i == toks.size()-1 (memcpy into last_logits); every other prefix logits row is computed and thrown away. SPAN decodes (lines 205-207) and full mode legitimately consume (nearly) all rows, so the waste is PREFIX-only. llama.cpp's n_outputs/inp_out_ids machinery computes the lm_head only for flagged rows and sizes the output buffer to the flagged count, so flagging everything really does cost extra compute (512x151936 vs 1x151936 projection per micro-batch) and forces the ~311 MB output buffer (512*151936*4 B, verified). FLOP fraction verified: Qwen2-0.5B body ~358M weights vs lm_head ~136M = ~27.6%, matching the claimed ~28%. Magnitude check against the shipped config: run_anomaly.py runs up to 6 languages x 6 windows = ~36 variants jobs with depths up to 45,000 bytes, i.e. ~13-15K prefix tokens per job dominating each job's decode, so roughly 28% of the anomaly stage's decode compute (~25-40 min on the 4-core budget) is wasted. One correction to the claim: the 16 ablation jobs are NOT affected — scripts/run_ablation.py uses run_full_window (mode=full), which needs all logits; only the anomaly stage uses variants mode, so the reviewer's 45-60 min estimate is roughly halved. No measurement corruption: discarded logits do not affect the KV cache, last_logits, or any emitted TSV value. Real efficiency/memory defect, correctly rated minor.

When logits_last_only is set, skip the per-token llama_get_logits_ith loop and instead fetch the single flagged row after the final micro-batch (llama_get_logits_ith with output index 0, or llama_get_logits) and invoke on_logits once for the last token — note llama_get_logits_ith indexes output rows, not batch positions, so the existing i - s indexing must not be used with sparse flags. This drops ~28% of PREFIX decode compute in the anomaly stage and shrinks the output buffer from ~311 MB to ~600 KB during prefix decodes. Apply only after the in-flight chained runs finish or accept the resumable jobs re-running; the change is compute-only and does not alter any emitted values.

confirmed.summary: read_manifest does json.loads on every non-blank line with no error handling, so a torn final line from a crash mid-append permanently blocks resume of the sweep/anomaly/ablation stages.
confirmed.failure_scenario: append_manifest writes rows with buffered f.write; if the process is SIGKILLed or the machine dies mid-write (the chain script explicitly anticipates 'sweep process died' and restarts it), the manifest can end with a partial JSON line. On restart, run_sweep.py/run_anomaly.py call read_manifest before doing anything, json.loads raises JSONDecodeError, and the run exits immediately — the auto-restart loop in chain_after_sweep.sh then respawns it every 60s into the same crash, stalling the remaining ~10h pipeline until someone hand-edits the manifest.

verdicts.reasoning: Traced end-to-end and confirmed mechanically. Write side: append_manifest (leanscale/runner.py:81-84) uses a buffered f.write with no fsync; sweep rows embed the full per-window file list (scripts/run_sweep.py:91) and can exceed the 8 KiB stdio buffer, so a SIGKILL/OOM-kill between the resulting multiple write(2) syscalls — or host death losing part of the page cache — persists a torn, newline-less partial JSON line. The chain script explicitly anticipates the sweep dying, so crashes are in-scope. Read side: read_manifest line 91 does json.loads on every non-blank line with no error handling; a torn line raises JSONDecodeError with no handler up-stack. All three resumable stages call read_manifest as their first real action (run_sweep.py:51, run_anomaly.py:46, run_ablation.py:49), so the restarted process exits within seconds. chain_after_sweep.sh's babysitter (lines 29-49) respawns it every 60s into the identical crash and, after 5 attempts (~5-6 min), prints SWEEP_FAILED and exits 1, so anomaly/ablation/quant-check never run — the remaining ~10 h pipeline stalls until someone hand-edits manifest.jsonl. The reviewer's scenario is accurate (minor correction: the loop gives up after 5 retries rather than looping forever, with the same net effect). Unlike the main curves.csv (which records n_windows per bin row), the code-only CSV rows (lines 254-256) omit any window count, and REPORT.md's 'Byte-class breakdown' table aggregates whatever remains and presents it as the per-language result, so a language whose code-only statistics come from a fraction of its windows is indistinguishable from a complete one.

rejected.summary: No per-job error handling and no token-budget guard on prefix depth: one window whose deepest prefix exceeds n_ctx aborts the entire anomaly sweep, and resume deterministically re-crashes on the same job.

llama.cpp is built with -DGGML_NATIVE=ON and the cached build is never revalidated on container restart (line 36 skips rebuild if libllama.so exists), so after the container was rescheduled onto a CPU without AVX-VNNI the cached libggml-cpu.so kills every ppl-dump decode with SIGILL — the running sweep is dead right now with only 2/70 windows measured.

The babysitter's restart loop burns its entire 5-restart budget in minutes on a deterministic per-window crash (no backoff, no check that a restart made new progress) and then permanently exits with SWEEP_FAILED, killing the whole 10h chain — this already happened at ~21:44 per chain.log, so anomaly/ablation/quant-check will never launch without manual relaunch.

Ablation comparison does not enforce per-window pairing: the annotated baseline set is filtered by baseline ids from ALL ablation-manifest rows while the stripped set is filtered by dump-file existence, so a missing/undumped window on either side silently compares different window sets.
